name: Pellucid BioClean Class-1 Geneware Lab Suit
description:
A cleanroom suit designed for Class-1 geneware fabrication environments and high-grade biotech labs. The outer shell is ultrasonic-welded polyethylene fabric in sterile white with fine silver anti-static threading — new suits are blinding white; worn ones carry a faint yellowish cast from sterilization fluid cycling. Hood is integrated with a sealed polycarbonate visor and positive-pressure filtered air delivery at the collar.

Every seam is smooth-faced inward to prevent particulate shedding. Gloves are separate but connect via sterile-lock ring cuffs. The suit design accommodates tail and horn geneware through sealed elasticated apertures at the base of the spine and crown — apertures ship sealed and are field-opened by the user. Used in Tier 4-5 labs but also smuggled into unlicensed Shelf geneware clinics.
functionality: Class-1 cleanroom rated — less than 10 particles per cubic foot. Positive-pressure air delivery prevents contaminant ingress. Anti-static threading prevents charge buildup near sensitive biotech equipment. Sealed gene-compatible apertures at spine base and crown. Neural port access panel at rear collar for BCI techs working in sterile environments.
what_it_says: You work with things precise enough that your body is the contamination risk.
manufacturer: Pellucid BioSystems (Tier 4-5 licensed); stolen/surplus units reach Shelf clinics
story_hooks: A Shelf geneware clinic is performing unlicensed modifications using stolen Pellucid suits — the suits are legitimate, but nothing else in the operating space is.
A lab technician notices their suit's positive-pressure system has been quietly downgraded — someone wanted a specific sample to get out of the cleanroom.
The sealed gene-apertures on a batch of suits were shipped pre-opened, suggesting someone at the factory is flagging suits for buyers who don't want to ask questions about their modifications.
